frequency_question: How often do states under wartime constraints successfully stand up domestic assembly for complex foreign cruise/precision missiles when initial advance signals (transfer of technical data packages, co-production agreements) are visible?
membership_rule: Includes sovereign states engaged in active interstate conventional war that transition from importing complex guided munitions (cruise missiles, anti-ship missiles) to domestic assembly or component manufacturing within a 3-year window. Excludes small arms, unguided artillery, or basic drone production.

cases.name: Iran domestic production of modified Fateh/Qods series from foreign designs under severe sanctions
Ukraine domestic attempt at Hrim-2 tactical missile finalization under wartime conditions
Taiwan domestic production scaling of Hsiung Feng cruise missile variants under constant PRC threat
Ukraine domestic production of Neptun anti-ship missile following initial design phase
Yemen (Houthi-held) local assembly/modifications of Iranian-supplied cruise missile components

coverage_note: 5 named cases representing major wartime high-tech missile localization efforts over the past two decades.
known_gaps: Classified nature of modern missile co-production agreements limits comprehensive enumeration of all clandestine bilateral transfers.
skeleton: Cases of localized high-tech missile manufacturing starts during active conflict or extreme technological isolation, where precursor technical agreements or component transfers were observed.
multiplier: 3 hits out of 5 observed analogous historical/contemporary technology transfer and wartime manufacturing transition cases.
validity_reason: The base rate reflects enduring constraints on defense industrial base transitions during wartime, which evolve slowly over multi-year technological eras.
